newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power higher after BPA pullout.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power higher after BPA pullout.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Northwest moved higher Thursday following the Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) decision not to offer surplus power in the next-day market, trade sources said.
"Both COB (California-Oregon border) and Mid-Co (Mid-Columbia) prices are up. With Bonneville out of the market, there is some scrambling around," said one trader.
Firm, peak power at COB for Friday was last quoted $21.00-22.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from the $18.50-19.50 level seen since early this week.
Friday on-peak Mid-Columbia deliveries were quoted near $21.00, up from $17.50-18.00.
BPA said it withdrew from the market due to recent above-normal regional demand and the need to let hydroelectric reservoir levels return to normal operating levels.
Recent strength in spot natural gas prices was also cited as helping to firm power prices.
"November gas prices are being pushed up because a lot of people are buying for storage," said one northern California trader. "But our loads are going down."

In the Southwest, Friday firm, on-peak deliveries at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona were little changed at $19.00-20.00, compared with $18.00-20.00 on Wednesday. Off-peak Palo Verde was quoted $12.00-13.00.
